examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Многие из вас = many of you. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('many (people)').

examples.text: У многих из вас появились сомнения.
examples.trans: Many of you have begun to have doubts.
Many people think the same way.

examples.text: У многих из вас появились сомнения. Хочу сказать вам.
examples.trans: Many of you have begun to have doubts. I want to tell you.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I used to come see you often.

examples.text: А меня не помнишь? Я Артурик, я к вам часто приходил.
examples.trans: And don't you remember me? I'm Arturik, I used to come see you often.

meanings.note: Появились сомнения = doubts arose. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'омнение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'doubt' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У многих из вас появились сомнения.
examples.trans: Many of you have begun to have doubts.
There is no doubt about that.

examples.text: У многих из вас появились сомнения. Хочу сказать вам.
examples.trans: Many of you have begun to have doubts. I want to tell you.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

насколько.gloss: how much, to what extent, as far as

meanings.note: in expressions like насколько я знаю / насколько нам известно

Interrogative or relative. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'сколько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Насколько нам известно, она закрыла долг.
examples.trans: As far as we know, she paid off the debt.

examples.text: Насколько нам известно, Марина Сергеевна полностью закрыла долг.
examples.trans: As far as we know, Marina Sergeyevna has paid off the debt in full.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рого'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Французские десерты всегда стоят очень дорого.
examples.trans: French desserts always cost very much.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'терять'.

examples.text: Что смотрите, бандерлоги? Вы совсем страх потеряли?
examples.trans: What are you staring at, you monkeys? Have you lost all fear?

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!
